## My thinking this season

I've been farming these 200 mu for forty years now, and with the kids grown and only four of us in the household, I rely on hired labor and my own machinery to get the work done. High school education gave me enough to read the agronomy pamphlets and do my own input calculations, so I don't just copy what the neighbors do — I plan based on soil tests I had done two years ago and what the market looks like.

Squash is my main cash crop — that's what pays for the diesel, the hired hands, and the fertilizer bills. I'll put 120 mu in squash this year because the buyer from Handan renewed the contract and the price held up last autumn. I keep 60 mu in wheat-maize double cropping because it's my insurance — steady yield, government purchase price, and the straw feeds back into the soil. The remaining 20 mu stays in millet on the sandier patch near the north edge where irrigation is weak; millet handles drought and I sell the grain plus use some for the family.

On nitrogen: I target based on expected yield. Wheat 500 kg/mu target means about 20 kg N/mu split base and topdress. Maize I push to 550 kg/mu with 18 kg N/mu. Squash gets more balanced NPK because potassium matters for fruit quality. Millet barely needs anything.

Irrigation: wells are metered and electricity isn't cheap, so I don't overdo it. Wheat gets 3 irrigations (green-up, jointing, grain-fill), maize 1-2 depending on summer rain, squash 4-5 because it's thirsty and high-value, millet 0-1.
